gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Macworld (Simon Jary, 2 Apr 2026), testing the Trio 3 Pro on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, found the two screens couldn't draw enough power from the laptop to reach full brightness and needed a power adapter plugged into the Trio. No result gives a figure any lab or named reviewer measured for any 14-inch extender candidate.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited rival pages. itechguides.com '15 Best Laptop Screen Extenders for 2026' has no lab or reviewer measurements: every brightness, gamut, weight and power figure in it comes from the maker or an Amazon seller. theofficejournal.com 'Best USB-C Laptop Screen Extenders' has no measured figures either, only listed weights (1.87 lb, 3.0 lb), and says nothing about brightness on laptop power. Neither page names a reviewer's finding on power-limited brightness or on which MacBooks need the driver for two added screens. The finding is a reviewer's observation, not a meter reading. No named measurement exists in what I could open for the Duex Max DS, FOPO S1/S7, UPERFECT 2K 14, Aura Dual Boost/Dual Go 14 or SideTrak Swivel 14. That keeps this at 2, not 3. Our own Trio 3 Pro record already cites Macworld for the 14-inch MacBook Pro test, so the after-section may already hold part of this.
decides: It confirms the Trio 3 Pro as the two-added-screen pick for a 14-inch laptop only with a caveat. On a 14-inch laptop powered only from its own USB-C, Macworld found the screens dim, and Android.com.pl (Łukasz Pająk) also says full brightness needs extra power. Budget for a USB-C power adapter on the Trio's pass-through port, which Macworld puts at up to 65 W to the laptop. Macworld also states that base M1 and M2 MacBooks need Mobile Pixels' free software to run both screens, while Pro/Max chips and M4/M5 run both without it. That supports the page's rule on each row's video path. Neither point changes the single-screen pick (Duex Max DS), which has no named measurement either way.

findings.label: Brightness when powered only by the laptop
findings.value: Screens could not reach maximum brightness on power from a 14-inch MacBook Pro; full brightness needs a power adapter in one of the Trio's USB-C ports (pass-through up to 65 W to the laptop)
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Reviewer's hands-on observation on a 14-inch MacBook Pro, not a meter reading. Quote: 'the Trio's screens can't draw enough power from the connected laptop to allow for maximum screen brightness'. He found the capped brightness acceptable. The 300 nits per screen in the review is Mobile Pixels' rating, not measured.

findings.label: Which MacBooks run both added screens
findings.value: Base M1 and M2 MacBooks (and MacBook Neo): one screen without software, both screens with Mobile Pixels' free software. M1/M2/M3 Pro and Max, and any M4 or M5 MacBook: both screens without the software
findings.source_title: Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro review (Macworld, Simon Jary, Apr 2, 2026)
findings.note: Macworld's statement in the review. It also cites the manual: no driver needed when the laptop has two DisplayPort-enabled USB-C ports. Macworld says the Trio fits 13–16-inch MacBooks; Mobile Pixels' own fit range in our record is 15–16 inches.

findings.label: Brightness on laptop power, second reviewer
findings.value: Full capability, including full brightness, needs extra power; brightness described as limited, fine indoors but not necessarily in strong sun; colour quality 'simply acceptable'
findings.source_title: Test Mobile Pixels Trio 3 Pro i Float 2 (Android.com.pl, Łukasz Pająk, 2026-08-25)
findings.note: Translated from Polish. Qualitative only: no instrument and no measured cd/m² or watts. The 300 nits, 100% sRGB, 1000:1 and 1.81 kg in its table are maker specs.

findings.product: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender (not a candidate, an older and smaller FOPO model)
findings.label: Measured panel results
findings.value: 185 cd/m² centre (177.4 cd/m² average, 85% uniformity), 247:1 contrast, 79% sRGB, 77.1% Display P3, Delta E 4.59 ColorChecker uncalibrated
findings.source_title: FOPO 12-inch triple monitor extender review: Clunky and more fragile than standalone portable monitors (Notebookcheck, Allen Ngo, 2022-07-23)
findings.note: Measured by Notebookcheck with an X-Rite i1Pro 2. This is the only named lab measurement of any FOPO extender I found. It is not the S1 or S7, uses a different panel size and is from 2022, so do not carry it to our FOPO rows. No power-draw or weight figure in the review.

unsourced: Measured brightness, gamut or power draw for the Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS. Searched for RTINGS, Notebookcheck, Tom's Hardware and TechRadar reviews: none found. Root-Nation's Duex Max DS review returned 403. The Mighty Gadget review returned 404 after its redirect.

Amateur Photographer's Spyder X2 gamut measurement of the original Duex Max (a search snippet says 64% sRGB). The page returned 403 at both URLs, so the figure is unverified. It is also the original Duex Max, not the DS.
TechPowerUp's 'Quick Look: Mobile Pixels DUEX Max' returned 403, so I couldn't check it for measurements.

A measured figure for the Trio 3 Pro: Macworld, Chip.pl and Android.com.pl list maker specs only. Chip.pl's 11 W power draw is from its spec table, not a meter. RTINGS has tested only the original 13-inch TRIO, and its review page didn't render.
Any named measurement of the FOPO S1 or FOPO S7. None found: Notebookcheck has reviewed only a 12-inch FOPO triple.
Any named measurement of the UPERFECT 2K 14-inch 360° swivel (2240×1400). The UPERFECT reviews I found cover other models (GR14BU OLED, UD14BQ pen display).
Any review with measurements of the Aura Dual Boost 14 or Aura Dual Go 14 Ultra. None found: TweakTown and AppleInsider covered the Triple Boost 14 Pro, a different model, and I didn't open them.

A measured figure for the SideTrak Swivel 14. The Gadgeteer's 14-inch review (Howard Sneider, 2024-01-01) gives only spec-list figures (340 cd/m², 1.5 lb, 4.75 W). A search snippet says Tom's Hardware measured about 301.4 nits, but on a 12.5-inch unit, and I didn't open that page.
Measured weight on a scale for any candidate. Macworld's 4.13 lb (1.9 kg) for the Trio 3 Pro doesn't say it was weighed and matches the spec.
